title: Build a One-Person Company OS
hook: You do not need more hustle. You need fewer dropped decisions.
outcome: A simple operating system connecting leads, work, cash, evidence, and learning.
steps: Create one source of truth for customers, offers, work, invoices, evidence, and next actions.
Define a weekly operating rhythm: sell, deliver, collect, support, review, improve.
Automate capture and reminders, not judgment-heavy decisions you have not standardized.
Use approval gates for messages, contracts, payments, purchases, and destructive actions.
Review the current constraint and one measurable next action every day.
cta: Follow for the complete one-person operator stack.
disclaimer: Automation should preserve accountability, security, consent, and recoverability.

title: Write an SOP in 20 Minutes
hook: A useful SOP is a tested path to an accepted outcome, not a wall of text.
outcome: A reusable procedure with inputs, actions, checks, and recovery.
steps: Name the outcome, owner, trigger, inputs, tools, and definition of done.
Record the real process once while doing it. Capture decisions and failure points.
Rewrite it as numbered actions with one action per step.
Add validation after risky steps plus rollback or escalation instructions.
Have another person—or future you—run it and update unclear sections.
cta: Comment SOP for the one-page template.
disclaimer: Keep credentials and sensitive customer data out of general documentation.

title: Build a Dashboard That Drives Action
hook: Reporting everything can hide the one thing blocking growth.
outcome: A weekly scorecard built around outcome, constraint, action, and learning.
steps: Choose one outcome metric that reflects real customer or business value.
Add three to five driver metrics you can influence this week.
Show target, actual, trend, source, owner, and data freshness.
Name the current constraint and the action expected to change it.
Record what happened, why, and what the next cycle will change.
cta: Save this before building another vanity dashboard.
disclaimer: Metrics can mislead when definitions or sources change. Keep a data dictionary.

title: Automate Your Weekly Business Review
hook: The review should arrive with evidence before motivation has a chance to disappear.
outcome: A scheduled operating report with anomalies, decisions, and next actions.
steps: Pull posted revenue, expenses, leads, deliveries, support issues, and key product usage from approved sources.
Calculate consistent metrics and flag missing or stale data instead of filling gaps.
Summarize wins, misses, anomalies, unresolved risks, and the largest constraint.
Generate proposed actions with owners and due dates, but require approval before external side effects.
Store each report so trends and decisions can be audited later.
cta: Comment REVIEW for the report schema.
disclaimer: Financial totals should state their coverage window and source limitations.
